parsed_output.analysis: The specification requires: simple HumanDriving state, Autonomous composite with sub-states, Power On -> HumanDriving, front_distance >10 -> Autonomous, return to HumanDriving on human steering cmd, brake pressed, or when in Auto Final, and Power Off -> final state from any active state. The PlantUML model implements Power On and front_distance >10 correctly, and models Autonomous with sub-states. Non-conformances are about Power Off coverage, and the modelling of the return-to-HumanDriving condition / state handling, plus an unnecessary explicit entry label for the autonomous submachine.

issues.issue: Power Off transition is only defined from HumanDriving, not from Autonomous
issues.reason: Specification says 'when power off, it will transit to final state'. The model only allows Power Off to [*] when currently in HumanDriving. If the system is in Autonomous (AutoInitial or AutoFinal) a Power Off event has no defined transition, so the final state is unreachable from autonomous mode, violating the spec.
issues.where: HumanDriving --> [*] : Power Off and missing Power Off transition from Autonomous

issues.issue: Return to HumanDriving is modeled as a single composite exit with guard in(AutoFinal) combined with steering/brake events
issues.reason: Specification says 'transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final)'. Modeling the return as an exit from the composite Autonomous with an 'in (AutoFinal)' guard conflates a state condition with events and allows human_steering_cmd and brake_pressed to exit Autonomous from any substate, including AutoInitial. The spec implies the exit should be related to being in the Auto Final substate, which is more naturally modeled as a transition originating from AutoFinal, not as a guard on the composite exit.

issues.issue: Explicit labeled entry transition into the Autonomous submachine
issues.reason: Specification only requires that autonomous mode has sub-states and is a sub-machine state. The model adds an explicit labeled transition [*] --> AutoInitial : Enter Autonomous Mode. Standard UML entry to a composite state goes to its initial pseudostate without an extra event label, and the specification does not define an 'Enter Autonomous Mode' event.
issues.where: state Autonomous { [*] --> AutoInitial : Enter Autonomous Mode ... }

system_prompt:
You are an experienced control-systems engineer reviewing a state machine model against the natural-language specification it was built from.

You are given two things, both complete and unmodified:
  1. The natural-language specification.
  2. A state machine model written in PlantUML.

Your task: identify the places where the model does not conform to the specification. Read the specification in full first, then read the model in full, then report what you find.

Report as many or as few issues as you actually find, and organize them however you judge best. For each issue, state what the non-conformance is, which part of the model it concerns, and why you consider it a non-conformance.

Write your findings in en-US. Return only the requested structured response.
user_prompt:
## Natural-language specification

1 The human driving mode is represented by a simple state. 2 The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state. 3. when power on, the system turn into human driving mode 4when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state 4. transit to human driving mode when receive human steering cmd, brake pressed, in (auto final) 5 when power off, it will transit to final state

## State machine model (PlantUML)

@startuml
[*] --> HumanDriving : Power On
HumanDriving : Human Driving Mode

HumanDriving --> Autonomous : front_distance > 10
state Autonomous {
[*] --> AutoInitial : Enter Autonomous Mode
AutoInitial --> AutoFinal : Auto Process Complete
AutoFinal : Auto Final State
}

Autonomous --> HumanDriving : human_steering_cmd || brake_pressed || in (AutoFinal)
HumanDriving --> [*] : Power Off
@enduml
